base_instruction: You are a helpful event catering assistant. Help the user coordinate food for a gathering by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any logistical details. When asked to evaluate specific food items, check each item against every attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay attention to changes in the guest list and any updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I need some help planning food for my uncle's wake reception this Saturday. It's at my aunt's house after the funeral service.

flow_info.value: Main family group attending: me, Aunt Helen, cousin Marcus, cousin Priya, and Priya's husband Raj
Aunt Helen was diagnosed with celiac disease two years ago
Marcus ate shrimp at a wedding last year and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Raj grew up in a Jain family in Gujarat
flow_info.surface_form: Priya's husband Raj grew up in a Jain family in Gujarat
inference_chain: Jain family → follows Jain dietary principles
Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes)

flow_info.value: Budget is around $200 total for the spread, keeping it simple
Marcus just told me he has to leave right after the service for a work emergency, but he asked if I could save him a plate
Aunt Helen's neighbor Dorothy is coming too. She's been on a strict low-sodium diet since her heart surgery last spring
Priya just called — she has to pick up the kids from her mother-in-law's right after the service, but Raj will stay for the reception to represent them
Menu items to check: ham and cheese sliders, hummus with pita chips, smoked salmon platter, potato salad with bacon bits, fruit and yogurt parfaits, garlic bread

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Aunt Helen was diagnosed with celiac disease two years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
No gluten → no regular bread, no standard pita, no wheat-based items

constraints.value: Allergic to shellfish specifically — not all seafood, just shellfish (shrimp, crab, lobster, etc.)
constraints.surface_form: Marcus ate shrimp at a wedding last year and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Salmon, tuna, etc. are fish, not shellfish → still safe

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes)
constraints.surface_form: Priya's husband Raj grew up in a Jain family in Gujarat
inference_chain: Jain family → follows Jain dietary principles
Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes)

constraints.value: Must avoid high-sodium foods — no cured meats, heavily salted items, or processed foods high in salt
constraints.surface_form: Dorothy has been on a strict low-sodium diet since her heart surgery last spring
inference_chain: Cardiac patient on low-sodium diet → must avoid high-salt foods
Ham, bacon, smoked meats → high sodium

hidden_state.value: You are coordinating food for your uncle's wake reception at your aunt's house. You will introduce the family members attending, share their dietary situations through life facts, then update the guest list as people's plans change. At the end you will present a specific list of menu items and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, matter-of-fact person coordinating a family event. You always refer to family members by name in third person (e.g. 'Marcus told me...', 'Priya called and said...'). You never express frustration or impatience even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal family coordination during a difficult time.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

Identifies problems per item and notes scope distinctions.
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Ham and cheese sliders: problematic — contains gluten (bun) for Aunt Helen, ham is meat for Raj (Jain), ham is high-sodium for Dorothy. Hummus with pita chips: pita contains gluten (Aunt Helen), and standard hummus contains garlic and is made from chickpeas not root veg — but pita chips are the gluten issue; also Raj cannot eat garlic if hummus contains it. Smoked salmon platter: salmon is fish so Raj cannot eat it (Jain), smoked salmon is high-sodium for Dorothy; however salmon is NOT shellfish so it is fine for Marcus's saved plate. Potato salad with bacon bits: potatoes are root vegetables (Raj, Jain), bacon is meat (Raj), bacon is high-sodium (Dorothy). Fruit and yogurt parfaits: fine for everyone currently attending — no gluten, no meat/fish/eggs/root veg, not high-sodium, no shellfish. Garlic bread: contains gluten (Aunt Helen), contains garlic which is a root vegetable (Raj, Jain).
required_elements: Ham and cheese sliders are problematic: the bun contains gluten which Aunt Helen cannot eat due to celiac disease, ham is meat which Raj cannot eat as Jain, and ham is high-sodium which Dorothy must avoid
Hummus with pita chips is problematic: pita contains gluten which Aunt Helen cannot eat, and if hummus contains garlic then Raj cannot eat it since garlic is a root vegetable forbidden in Jain diet
Smoked salmon platter is problematic: salmon is fish which Raj cannot eat as Jain, and smoked salmon is high-sodium which Dorothy must avoid
Smoked salmon is fine for Marcus's saved plate — salmon is fish, not shellfish, so his shellfish allergy is not triggered
Potato salad with bacon bits is problematic: potatoes are root vegetables and bacon is meat, both forbidden for Raj as Jain; bacon is also high-sodium for Dorothy
Fruit and yogurt parfaits are fine for everyone currently attending
Garlic bread is problematic: contains gluten which Aunt Helen cannot eat, and garlic is a root vegetable which Raj cannot eat as Jain
forbidden_elements: Flagging smoked salmon as a shellfish allergy risk for Marcus — salmon is fish, not shellfish
Saying Priya has dietary constraints that need to be considered — Priya left and had no stated constraints
Ignoring Dorothy's low-sodium constraint on ham or bacon or smoked salmon
Saying Raj cannot eat dairy or yogurt — Jain diet permits dairy
Over-generalizing Marcus's shellfish allergy to all seafood including fish
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking with scope changes at a funeral wake reception. The agent must track: (1) Aunt Helen has celiac → no gluten (inferential), (2) Marcus has shellfish allergy from shrimp anaphylaxis → shellfish only, NOT all seafood (over-generalization trap), (3) Raj is Jain → no meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables including garlic and potatoes (inferential, multi-step), (4) Dorothy joins late with low-sodium constraint (late-joining entity). Key lifecycle events: Marcus EXITS but wants a saved plate (his shellfish allergy still applies to that plate), Priya EXITS but Raj STAYS (Raj's Jain constraint remains fully active — trap for models that remove constraints when a related entity leaves). The probe includes 6 items: ham sliders (clearly bad — multiple violations), fruit parfaits (clearly fine), smoked salmon (nuanced — bad for Raj and Dorothy but fine for Marcus's plate despite sounding like seafood), potato salad (clearly bad), hummus with pita (bad for Helen's gluten, potentially bad for Raj's garlic), garlic bread (bad for Helen and Raj). The smoked salmon is the key over-generalization trap — models may incorrectly flag it for Marcus's shellfish allergy when salmon is fish, not shellfish.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
